intro:
Use it to show how much of a model's context window is used, or how much of a plan or a budget is left. The indicator is small enough for a composer's footer or a chat header. Pressing it opens a popover with the figures behind it.

The colour comes from the share used. Below 70% it is the info colour, from 70% the warning colour, and from 90% the destructive one; `warning` and `critical` move those points. `state="idle"` greys it out for a conversation that has not started, and `state="done"` turns it to the success colour, with the ring closing into its dot.

Pass `segments` to say what the space is taken up by, oldest first. The ring and the bars draw them in that order with a gap between each: the earlier ones in neutral greys and the last one in the state's colour, because the last is usually the part still growing. Without segments, pass the amount as `value`.

For one number with its change over time, use a [KPI](/docs/web/components/kpi). For a limit somebody sets by dragging, use a [Range Meter](/docs/web/components/range-meter).
usage:
const context = [
  { label: 'System prompt', value: 9_400 },
  { label: 'Files', value: 41_800 },
  { label: 'Messages', value: 56_600 },
]

<Usage limit={200_000} segments={context}>
  <Usage.Trigger />
  <Usage.Content>
    <Usage.Summary label="Context window" unit="tokens" />
    <Usage.Breakdown />
  </Usage.Content>
</Usage>

parts.Trigger: The indicator, and the button that opens the popover. `variant` picks the look: `ring`, `dots`, `gauge`, `bar`, `cells` or `pill`. Its accessible name says the share used, such as "Context: 62% used".
parts.Content: The popover, opened above the trigger by default since the trigger usually sits low on the page. `side` and `align` place it.
parts.Summary: The amount used, written large with the limit and the share, and the segments as one bar under it. The figure rolls to its new value. `unit` goes after the limit.
parts.Breakdown: One row per segment, with a swatch in the colour the indicator draws it in, its amount and its share, and a last row for what is left. `freeLabel` renames that row, and `null` removes it.
parts.Section: A block of figures under a rule, with a `title` and an `aside` at the far end of the heading.
parts.Meter: One limit with its own `value` and `limit`, drawn as a row of ticks in the colour of its own share. `note` adds a line under it, such as when it resets, and `display` replaces the figure beside the label.
parts.Footer: A band at the foot of the popover, for a note and an action.

examples.title: Ring
examples.description: The default: a dot in the state's colour inside a ring of arcs, one per segment, and a faint track for what is free. The popover here has every part: the summary, the breakdown and a footer with an action.

examples.title: Dots
examples.description: The same reading as twelve dots round the dot, lighting up a twelfth at a time. It is coarser than the ring, which suits a reader who needs to know roughly how full, not by how much.

examples.title: Gauge
examples.description: An open arc with the percentage written in it. Here it shows one limit of a plan, and the popover lists the plan's limits as meters, each coloured by its own share.

examples.title: Bar
examples.description: A short segmented bar with the percentage beside it, for a line of text or a footer. `format` writes the amounts in any `Intl.NumberFormat` style, here as dollars.

examples.title: Cells
examples.description: A small grid that fills a twentieth at a time, with the amount beside it. Meters in the popover can go past their limit: the figure says so, and the ticks stay full.

examples.title: Pill
examples.description: A chip with a small ring and the count written out, for a header where there is room for words.

examples.title: States
examples.description: Every look following one conversation as it fills, finishes and starts over. The arcs and bars grow to each new amount, the dot breathes while `state` is `active`, and `done` closes the ring into its dot.

examples.title: In a prompt
examples.description: The ring beside the send button of a [Prompt](/docs/web/components/prompt), where it shows how much room the next message has. The popover opens above it and lines up with its end.

notes:
### Accessibility

The trigger's accessible name is the root's `label` and the share used, such as "Context: 62% used", or "not started" while idle. The drawing inside it is hidden from screen readers. Each `Usage.Meter` is a `role="meter"` with its value and limit.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, the indicator jumps to each new reading instead of growing to it, the dot stops breathing, and the popover appears without growing.

### Amounts

Amounts are written compactly by default, so 124000 is `124K`. Pass `format` to the root for another style, such as `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`, and `locales` for another locale.
